top.headline: The Fed Raises Interest Rates for the First Time Since 2023
top.blurb: The Federal Reserve voted to raise its benchmark rate a quarter point to a range of 3.75-4%, its first hike in three years, as the Iran war pushes energy and diesel prices higher. Two-thirds of the Fed's own policymakers expect at least one more hike before the year is out.

top.headline: House Holds Billionaire Leon Black in Contempt Over Epstein Probe
top.blurb: The House voted, with bipartisan support, to hold private-equity billionaire Leon Black in contempt of Congress for defying subpoenas in the Jeffrey Epstein investigation. It is the first contempt vote of the inquiry; the Justice Department must now decide whether to pursue criminal charges carrying up to a year in prison.

top.headline: Karnataka Minister Asks Why Modi and Shah Won't Try Umar Khalid
top.blurb: Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge challenged the Centre to finally put jailed student activist Umar Khalid on trial, asking what the government is afraid of. Khalid has been held without trial under the UAPA since 2020 over the Delhi riots case.

top.headline: Telangana CM Accuses KCR's Family of Illegal Land Holdings
top.blurb: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy told the Assembly that former chief minister K Chandrashekar Rao's family owns land far above the ceiling set by the state's land reforms law. The allegation escalates a running feud between the ruling Congress and the opposition BRS over the Rao family's assets.

top.headline: Gold Mine Collapse Kills at Least 70 in Sudan
top.blurb: A series of adjoining shafts collapsed at an artisanal gold mine in Sudan's West Kordofan state, killing at least 70 miners with dozens more trapped. No specialised rescue teams have joined the effort in the RSF-controlled area, and residents are digging survivors out of loose sand by hand.

top.headline: Rwanda and DRC Return to Geneva to Test a Fragile Peace Deal
top.blurb: Officials from Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo returned to Geneva to test whether last year's Washington peace accords can actually hold. Fighting between Congolese forces and the M23 rebel group continues in the eastern provinces the group seized, even as protesters at home push back against the president's bid for a third term.

top.headline: Harry Brook's Fastest T20I Century Demolishes Sri Lanka
top.blurb: England captain Harry Brook smashed an unbeaten 114 off 42 balls, his second T20I century, as England posted 254 for 4. Sri Lanka were bowled out for 135 in reply, handing England a 119-run win in the series opener at the Utilita Bowl.

top.headline: Are We Living Through a 'Baddies Revolution'?
top.blurb: NPR's It's Been a Minute examines how the Zeus Network's Baddies franchise, built on young women partying and fighting on camera, has quietly become one of reality TV's most influential exports. Scholar Donnetrice Allison joins to unpack what the show's popularity says about what its young cast believes is possible for themselves.

bengal.headline: Election Commission to Hear Rival Trinamool Factions Over Party Symbol
bengal.blurb: The Election Commission is separately hearing the Mamata Banerjee and Ritabrata Banerjee camps in Delhi to decide who controls the Trinamool Congress's "twin flowers" symbol ahead of Bengal's upcoming by-polls.

bengal.headline: Bengal Finishes First Phase of Census Fieldwork Ahead of Deadline
bengal.blurb: West Bengal completed houselisting across all 1.73 lakh census blocks before the September 14 deadline, enumerating nearly 3.68 crore houses, or about 99.7% of the projected total.

travel.headline: The Best Fall Road Trips Across the US and Canada
travel.blurb: From Minnesota's North Shore, where inland maples and lakeside birches turn on a delay, to Nova Scotia's roller-coaster Cabot Trail, Lonely Planet rounds up the drives that catch autumn at its peak.

travel.headline: A Congolese NGO Will Manage a DRC Nature Reserve for the First Time
travel.blurb: Strong Roots, a Congolese conservation group, has been handed a 10-year mandate to co-manage the Itombwe Nature Reserve, a 760,000-hectare sanctuary for Grauer's gorillas and nearly 600 bird species in South Kivu.

happy.headline: The Shipwreck Full of Champagne and Meteorites Meant for a Czar
happy.blurb: A ship that sank in the Baltic Sea around 1856, likely a gift convoy bound for Tsar Alexander II, is still giving up its cargo of champagne, mineral water and rare meteorites that never reached St. Petersburg.

tech_top.headline: OpenAI Backs a Bill Requiring Outside Safety Audits of AI Models
tech_top.blurb: OpenAI is publicly supporting a provision of the bipartisan FRONTIER Act that would require leading AI labs to let independent verification organizations inspect their models for safety. It is the first time the company has backed a federal AI safety mandate outright.
tech_top.pm_note: Worth tracking if you ship AI features: third-party model audits may go from optional trust signal to compliance requirement.

tech_top.headline: AI Safety Groups Have Quietly Built a Big Capitol Hill Lobbying Operation
tech_top.blurb: Billionaire-backed AI safety organizations like ControlAI have ramped up lobbying in Washington, holding hundreds of meetings with lawmakers. The push comes as Congress weighs how aggressively to regulate frontier AI development ahead of the midterms.
tech_top.pm_note: The regulatory timeline for AI product decisions may be moving faster in DC than most roadmaps assume.

tech_top.headline: Apple Folds Apple TV and Arcade Into iCloud+ at No Extra Cost
tech_top.blurb: Every paid iCloud+ tier, even the cheapest 50GB plan, now includes Apple TV and Apple Arcade free in more than 100 countries. The US, UK and most of Europe are notably excluded, with the rollout instead spanning Africa, Asia, the Middle East and Latin America.
tech_top.pm_note: A clean example of bundling as a retention lever: fold two underused subscriptions into one people already pay for.

tech_101.text: A proposed outside body that would get access to an AI company's model before release to check it for safety risks, similar to how auditors check a company's books.
Organized efforts, often funded by tech billionaires themselves, to persuade lawmakers to pass rules governing how AI models are built, tested and released.

science.headline: A Solar Desalination Device Turns Seawater to Fresh Water Without Toxic Brine
science.blurb: University of Rochester engineers built a solar-powered desalination device using laser-etched 'black metal' that wicks seawater upward, leaving salts and minerals behind as a solid rather than the concentrated brine that usually fouls coastlines. The self-cleaning system could even make it economical to recover lithium from the leftover salt.

science.headline: A Near-Perfect Engine Burn Doubles the Roman Space Telescope's Lifespan
science.blurb: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope used less than 10% of its budgeted fuel on its first course-correction burn, executed with over 99% accuracy. The leftover fuel could stretch its mission from an original ten years to as long as 22.

science.headline: The Flesh-Eating Screwworm the US Eradicated in 1982 Is Back
science.blurb: The New World screwworm, a parasitic fly whose larvae burrow into living flesh, has reached Texas and New Mexico decades after a mass eradication campaign wiped it out. Researchers are racing to revive that strategy before the pest re-establishes itself in US livestock and wildlife.

philosophy.headline: How to Fix What Indoctrination Breaks in Our Thinking
philosophy.blurb: Philosophers distinguish indoctrination from education by what it does to a person's capacity to reason: it doesn't just install false beliefs, it disables the tools that would let someone question them. The piece asks what actually rebuilds that capacity once it's gone.

philosophy.headline: The Unsettling Idea That Your Mind Is Just Along for the Ride
philosophy.blurb: Epiphenomenalism holds that consciousness is a byproduct of physical brain processes with no causal power of its own; your thoughts don't move your body, they just come along for the ride. It's one of philosophy's least comforting answers to the mind-body problem, precisely because so much of it appears consistent with the science.

philosophy_101.text: The view that mental states like thoughts and feelings are caused by brain activity but have no effect on it in return: consciousness as a passenger, not a driver.
